newsitem.title: PERU: Zinc price pushes Lima stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Zinc price pushes Lima stocks to higher close.

text.p: Lima shares rose slightly Wednesday, led by mining stocks that benefited from the rising price of zinc, now at $1.480 per tonne, brokers said.

Analysts expected the market to continue gaining Friday, dominated by local brokers investing in zinc-producing companies and the construction sector, which saw year-on-year growth of 18.3 percent in May.

According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index .IGRA climbed 0.58 percent to 2,229.03 points, while the blue-chip selective index .ISEL also rose 0.48 percent to 3,227.10 points.
According to preliminary market figures, 37.2 million soles ($14 million) was traded in 2,034 transactions.
The impetus present at the beginning of the market died mid-day when U.S. investors took off early ahead of Friday's Independence Day national holiday.
Brokers expected rises Friday due to the attractive prices and good fundamentals of certain stocks, and encouraging new economic growth figures.

The National Institute for Statistics and Information (INEI) released Thursday its monthly figures on economic growth, showing Peru's year-on-year growth for May was 7.2 percent, compared to 1.1 percent last year.
Also, year-on-year growth from January to May of this year was 7.2 percent compared to 2.5 percent last year.

"The market appears attractive for investors because the economy of this country is very strong," said analyst Carlos Patron from Peruval. "For the moment, this carries more weight more than political problems," he added, referring to the growing opposition to President Alberto Fujimori's government.
Patron said that the shares leading the bolsa were the polymetallic companies due to the increasing price for zinc on the international market.
The shares of mining companies Morococha, Milpo and Perubar rose 5.76 percent to 7.53 soles, 5.0 percent to 44.10 soles and 3.65 percent to 7,95 soles respectively.
"The construction sector as well is very attractive because demand for work increases as the economy of the country improves," said Patron.
The shares of construction company Cementos Lima climbed 0.19 percent to 5.37 soles.
The market leader Telefnica del Peru fell 0.57 percent to 6.96 soles.
